changes.text: 魏安釐王二十年，秦军围邯郸，魏王遣晋鄙救赵，平原君的使者责问魏救不至。魏公子决意赴秦军而死，路过夷门辞别后又折返，被一个守门老人当面点破：那是拿肉投餒虎。本文看他如何在没有干净选项时准备、付代价、认亏欠。

In the twentieth year of King Anxi of Wei, Qin's armies closed around Handan and the king of Wei sent General Jin Bi to relieve Zhao; Lord Pingyuan's envoys complained that Wei's relief had not come. The Wei prince resolved to go and die at the Qin army; after taking his leave at the Yimen gate and riding off, he turned back, and an old gatekeeper told him to his face that this was meat thrown to a starving tiger. Here is how he worked the problem when no option was clean — what he prepared, what it cost, and what he admitted he owed.
魏安釐王二十年，秦军击破赵长平军之后，进兵围住邯郸。魏王派将军晋鄙带十万众救赵。平原君的使者冠盖相属，赶到大梁责让魏公子：邯郸旦暮之间就要降秦，而魏国的救兵至今不到，公子不是自命能急人之困吗？末了还添一句「獨不憐公子姊邪」。魏公子的姐姐，正是平原君夫人。

In the twentieth year of King Anxi of Wei, after Qin had broken Zhao's army at Changping, its armies pressed on and encircled Handan. The king of Wei sent General Jin Bi with a hundred thousand troops to relieve Zhao. Envoys from Lord Pingyuan arrived in Daliang one after another — caps of office and carriage canopies in an unbroken line — reproaching the Wei prince: Handan was within days of surrendering to Qin, and Wei's relief still had not come; was the prince not the man who prided himself on rushing to others in distress? They added, in translation: had he no pity for his own sister? The prince's elder sister was Lord Pingyuan's wife.
此时公子手里只有三千门客，却未被任以国政。他决意赴秦军而死。出城路过夷门时，他向守门的侯生辞决。

At this point the prince had three thousand retainers but no appointment to the governance of the state. The plan he settled on was to go and die at the Qin army. On his way out of the city, passing the Yimen gate, he took his leave of Hou Ying, the gatekeeper.
魏公子在魏国的名声，一半来自养客。《史记》说他「公子為人仁而下士，士無賢不肖皆謙而禮交之」，不敢以富贵骄士，以致食客三千人，方圆数千里的士人争相投奔。这些门客不只是排场：有一回他和魏王下棋，北境举烽报警，说赵寇将入界，公子说是赵王田猎，不久北边传话果然如此。魏王问何以知晓，他说门客中有人能得赵王阴事。

The Wei prince's standing in Wei rested half on his retainers. The Grand Historian writes, in translation, that he was humane and humble toward men of talent, treating every scholar, worthy or not, with courtesy and respect, never presuming on wealth and rank — so that he had three thousand retainers, and men of ability from a radius of several thousand li competed to attach themselves to him. They were not mere pageantry. One day, while he was playing a board game with the king of Wei, beacon fires on the northern frontier signaled a Zhao raid about to cross the border. The prince said the king of Zhao was out hunting, nothing more. Word later came from the north confirming exactly that. Asked how he knew, he explained that among his retainers was a man who could ferret out the king of Zhao's private business.
一种解释是，这件事两面都算数：公子的信息能力得到验证，代价也记在账上——「是後魏王畏公子之賢能，不敢任公子以國政」。他越能干，魏王越不敢把国政交给他。等到邯郸告急，他未被任以国政，调兵无从谈起（作者推断）。

One reading is that the episode cuts both ways. His intelligence was proven — and the price went straight onto the ledger: in translation, from then on the king of Wei feared the prince's ability and dared not entrust him with the government of the state. The more capable he appeared, the less his king would hand him. By the time Handan cried for help he held no charge of the governance of the state, and raising troops was out of the question (the author's inference).
公子敬重的另一个人，在夷门。侯嬴年七十，家贫，做大梁夷门的守门人。公子要厚赠，他不肯受，说自己「脩身絜行數十年，終不以監門困故而受公子財」。公子于是置酒大会宾客，空出车左的上位，亲自驾车去迎。侯生穿着破旧衣冠，径直上车坐了上座，不让，公子执辔愈恭。到家引他坐上座、遍赞宾客，满座皆惊。

The other man the prince honored kept the Yimen, a gate of Daliang. Hou Ying was seventy, poor, and gatekeeper there. The prince called on him and wanted to make him a handsome gift, but he would not accept: in translation, he said he had kept himself and his conduct clean for decades and would not take the prince's money just because a gatekeeper's life left him poor. So the prince laid on a feast for his assembled guests, and when everyone was seated he drove out himself with his carriage and escort, leaving the seat of honor at the left of the carriage empty, to fetch Hou Ying in person. The old man turned up in his shabby clothes and worn cap, climbed straight into the seat of honor without yielding it, while the prince held the reins ever more respectfully. At home he seated Hou Ying in the place of honor and introduced him one by one to the assembled guests. The whole company was astonished.
侯生后来把话说穿：他故意让公子的车骑久立市中，让过客围观，公子愈恭，于是「市人皆以嬴為小人，而以公子為長者能下士也」。他还推荐过一位屠者朱亥，说「此子賢者，世莫能知」。公子几次登门去请，朱亥不回谢，公子当时只觉得奇怪。作者认为，这些看似闲棋的往来，邯郸被围那年全用上了。

Hou Ying later spelled out the game he had been playing. He had deliberately left the lord's carriage standing in the marketplace so that passers-by could watch: the longer the lord waited, the more deferential he became — and so, he said in translation, the townsfolk all took him for a petty man, and the lord for a true elder who could humble himself before men of talent. He also recommended a butcher named Zhu Hai, calling him, in translation, a worthy man whom the world did not know. The prince called on Zhu Hai several times; the butcher never came to return the courtesies, which the prince at that point simply found odd. In the author's view, all of these seemingly idle moves came due in the year Handan was besieged.
平原君的使者在大梁把话说绝：救兵不到，公子的高义安在。他决意赴秦军而死。
Lord Pingyuan's envoys left nothing to the imagination in Daliang: with no relief army in sight, where was the lord's famed righteousness? He resolved to go and die against the Qin army.
那天他出城，路过夷门，见到侯生，把要去秦军送死的打算讲了，辞决而行。侯生只说一句「公子勉之矣，老臣不能從」。车行数里，公子心不快——这是《史记》的叙述用语——说：「吾所以待侯生者備矣，天下莫不聞，今吾且死而侯生曾無一言半辭送我，我豈有所失哉？」他「復引車還，問侯生」。

That day he rode out, passed the Yimen gate, stopped to see Hou Ying and told him the whole plan — going to die at the Qin army — then took his leave and set off. Hou Ying said only, in translation, that the lord should push on, and that this old servant could not follow him. A few li on, the lord felt displeased — the narrator's own phrase — and said, in translation, that he had treated Hou Ying handsomely in every way, as all the world knew; now he was going to his death, and Hou Ying had not half a word to see him off — had he fallen short somewhere? So he turned his carriage around and went back to question Hou Ying.
作者认为，这一折返是全篇的转折。侯生当面把话挑明：「今有難，無他端而欲赴秦軍，譬若以肉投餒虎，何功之有哉」——没有别的办法，只想冲进秦军，等于拿肉喂饿虎，白送，还要门客何用。他还说，公子待他厚，此去而他不相送，公子必会「恨之復返」。他自己说：「以是知公子恨之復返也」。

In the author's reading, that turn is the pivot of the whole story. Hou Ying put it to his face, in translation: with disaster upon him and no other plan, the lord meant to throw himself at the Qin army — like throwing meat to a starving tiger; what would it accomplish? Nothing gained — and what use, then, are retainers? He added that the lord had treated him well, and he had not seen the lord off; from this, he said, he had known the lord would resent it and come back.
侯生给出的方案：他说，晋鄙的兵符常在魏王卧内，如姬最幸，出入卧内，有办法窃取。他又说，如姬的父亲被人所杀，三年未能报仇，自王以下想替她报父仇的都没能做到；她曾向公子泣诉，公子使客斩了仇人的头敬献给她。侯生说如姬「欲為公子死，無所辭，顧未有路耳」，所以公子开口请她，她必许。得虎符、夺晋鄙军，北救赵而西却秦，「此五霸之伐也」。

Hou Ying's plan, as he laid it out: Jin Bi's army tally — a tiger tally — was normally kept in the king of Wei's bedchamber, and Lady Ruji, the king's favorite, came and went there and was able to steal it. He went on: her father had been murdered; for three years she had sought revenge, and no one, from the king down, had been able to avenge him. She had wept to the prince, who sent a retainer to cut off her enemy's head and presented it to her respectfully. Hou Ying said she was ready to die for the prince and would refuse him nothing; only, in translation, she had not yet had the opportunity. If the prince would but ask, she would certainly agree. Then, with the tiger tally in hand, he could seize Jin Bi's army, relieve Zhao in the north and drive Qin back in the west — in translation, an achievement to rank with the Five Hegemons.

计策只管前半，后半是坏情况。侯生提醒「將在外，主令有所不受」：就算合符成功，晋鄙不交兵权、再向魏王请示，事情就危险了。带上屠者朱亥，「晉鄙聽，大善；不聽，可使擊之」。公子听完流泪，说「晉鄙嚄唶宿將，往恐不聽，必當殺之，是以泣耳，豈畏死哉」——哭的是非杀本国老将不可，不是怕死。朱亥说自己是市井鼓刀屠者，从前不回谢是以为小礼无所用，「今公子有急，此乃臣效命之秋也」。侯生此前已说过老臣不能从，这里只请数着公子的行程，到晋鄙军那天「北鄉自剄，以送公子」。

The plan covered only the first half; the second half was the bad case. Hou Ying warned, in translation, that a general in the field does not accept every order from his sovereign: even with the tallies matching, if Jin Bi withheld the army and sent to the king instead, the whole enterprise would be in danger. So take the butcher Zhu Hai along: if Jin Bi obeyed, excellent; if not, Zhu Hai could be made to strike him. The prince wept on hearing it; in translation, he said Jin Bi was a battle-seasoned old general who he feared would not obey, and then he would have to be killed — that was why he wept, not because he feared death. What he cried for was the killing of his own country's veteran commander, not the risk to himself. Zhu Hai said he was a butcher who wielded the knife in the marketplace; he had never returned the prince's visits because he thought petty courtesies were of no use — but now that the prince was in need, this was his moment to give his life. Hou Ying, who had already said at the gate that he could not follow, here only asked to count the days of the journey, so that on the day the prince reached Jin Bi's camp he would face north and cut his own throat, to see him off.
朱亥袖中四十斤铁椎，椎杀晋鄙。公子遂将晋鄙军，随即勒兵下令：「父子俱在軍中，父歸；兄弟俱在軍中，兄歸；獨子無兄弟，歸養。」得选兵八万人，进兵击秦军。

Zhu Hai, with a forty-catty iron mallet in his sleeve, struck Jin Bi dead. The prince then took command of Jin Bi's army and immediately issued an order to the troops, here in translation: where father and son were both serving, the father should go home; where brothers were both serving, the elder should go home; an only son with no brothers should go home and support his parents. He selected eighty thousand men and advanced against the Qin army.
秦军解去，邯郸得救，赵国保住。赵王与平原君亲到边界迎接，平原君背着箭袋在前引路，赵王再拜说「自古賢人未有及公子者也」，平原君不敢自比于人。

The Qin army broke off and withdrew. Handan was relieved, Zhao preserved. The king of Zhao and Lord Pingyuan came out to the border to receive him in person, Lord Pingyuan carrying the quiver and arrow-case and leading the way. The king of Zhao bowed twice and said, in translation, that of worthies since ancient times none had been the prince's equal. At that moment Lord Pingyuan dared not compare himself with anyone.
赵孝成王感念公子矫夺晋鄙兵存赵，与平原君商量以五城相封。公子的反应是「意驕矜而有自功之色」——仍是叙述用语。门客劝他：别人对公子的恩不可忘，公子对别人的恩最好忘掉；况且矫魏王令、夺晋鄙兵救赵，「於趙則有功矣，於魏則未為忠臣也」，自骄而居功，不可取。公子立自责，似若无所容者。

King Xiaocheng of Zhao, grateful that the prince had seized Jin Bi's army on a forged royal order and saved Zhao, took counsel with Lord Pingyuan about granting him five cities. The prince's reaction, in the narrator's phrasing (here in translation), was a look of pride and self-congratulation. A retainer told him: some things must not be forgotten, others must be. Kindness done to the prince he should remember; kindness the prince had done to others, he should forget. And besides, forging the king of Wei's order and seizing Jin Bi's army to save Zhao was, in translation, a service to Zhao but not the act of a loyal minister to Wei — to swagger over such a credit was beneath him. The prince at once blamed himself, looking as if he had nowhere to hide.
魏王怒公子盗兵符、矫杀晋鄙，公子自己清楚。退秦存赵之后，他让将领把军队带回魏国，自己与门客留在赵国。这场救赵中盗符夺军、矫杀晋鄙的一段没有魏王的授权。

The king of Wei was furious that the prince had stolen his tally and killed Jin Bi on a forged order, and the prince knew it. Having driven off Qin and saved Zhao, he sent the generals back to Wei with the army and stayed behind in Zhao with his retainers. The part of the rescue of Zhao in which he stole the tally, seized the army and killed Jin Bi carried no royal authorization.
作者认为，把整件事拆开看，公子一次也不是在好与坏之间挑，摆在面前的是两条都不干净的路：赴秦军而死（侯生斥为「以肉投餒虎」）、矫令夺军（侯生所献，伤本国）。作者推断，侯生那句「以肉投餒虎」的作用，是逼他把勇气换成方案。作者提出的反事实：若他不折返，多半死在秦军阵前，邯郸未必得救，也不会有后来那支进兵的军队。

In the author's reading, take the whole affair apart and the prince is never choosing between good and bad; what stood before him were two courses of action, both dirty: ride to die at the Qin army (which Hou Ying called throwing meat to a starving tiger), or forge an order and seize the army (proposed by Hou Ying; a wound to his own state). The author's inference is that Hou Ying's line about throwing meat to a starving tiger is what forced him to trade courage for a plan. The author's counterfactual: had he not turned back, he would most likely have died in front of the Qin lines, Handan might never have been relieved, and there would have been no army marching against Qin afterward.
第二处是把坏情况写进计划。侯生提醒将在外、主令有所不受，于是朱亥随行、袖中藏椎，晋鄙听则已，不听则击。作者推断，这一步的难处不在敢不敢：公子听后的反应是流泪说，怕晋鄙不听，到时必须杀他，自己并非怕死。从结果看，他欠了自己这方一笔债——杀本国宿将、盗王符、惹魏王怒——仍然把方案走完。原文未写他事前是否权衡，能记的只有这句答话。

The second undignified spot is writing the bad case into the plan. Hou Ying's reminder that a general in the field need not accept every order put Zhu Hai at his side with a mallet up his sleeve: if Jin Bi complied, well; if not, strike. The author's inference: the hard part here was not daring. The prince's response on hearing the plan was tears — he said he feared Jin Bi would not obey, and that he would then have to be killed, and that he was not afraid to die. In the outcome he took on a debt to his own side — killing his country's veteran commander, stealing the king's tally, angering the king — and he went through with it anyway. Whether he weighed this beforehand goes unrecorded; the only thing on the record is that answer.
第三处是事后的账。门客那句「於趙則有功矣，於魏則未為忠臣也」把两边算清：功劳是赵国的，亏欠是魏国的。原文只记他立自责，未记辩解之辞；另记退秦存赵之后，他遣军归魏、自己与门客留赵。作者推断，这是用离开把这笔债认下来（原文只写留赵这一行为，也未交代它与五城之议、自责孰先孰后）。一种解释是，他先有居功之色，受劝后立即自责，这一转与留赵相呼应：赵王、平原君边界亲迎在前，门客劝谏、公子自责在后。

The third is the accounting afterward. The retainer's words — in translation, a service to Zhao but not the act of a loyal minister to Wei — keep both columns straight: the credit belongs to Zhao, the debt to Wei. The source records only that he blamed himself on the spot, and nothing of any argument; it also records that, once Qin was driven off and Zhao saved, he sent the army home to Wei and stayed in Zhao with his retainers. The author infers that this acknowledged the debt through departure (the source records only the act of staying in Zhao, and does not say whether it came before or after the five-city offer and the self-reproach). One reading: he first showed a look of self-congratulation, then blamed himself at once when rebuked, and this turn chimes with his staying in Zhao — the welcome at the border came first, the retainer's rebuke and the self-reproach after.
先说史源。本篇只有一个来源——《史记·魏公子列传》一篇，无旁证可对。文中的对话与献计，如侯嬴献窃符之计、朱亥答话，是史家的记述，未必逐字。公子的「心不快」「意驕矜」「立自責」都是叙述用语，不是实录的心理。纪年照原文写魏安釐王二十年，不换算公元。

Start with the sources. This piece rests on a single source: the Biography of the Wei Prince in the Records of the Grand Historian, with no corroboration to set against it. The dialogue and the proposed scheme — Hou Ying's plan to steal the tally, Zhu Hai's reply — are the historian's rendering and need not be verbatim. The prince's displeasure, self-congratulation and self-blame, as the narrative describes them, are narrative labels, not recorded psychology. The year is given as the twentieth of King Anxi of Wei, as the source has it, with no conversion to the common era.
细节上更该存疑的是：「得選兵八萬人」这个数字只此一处，无旁证；晋鄙军中合符如何校验，原文没有记载；侯生自刭的动机，原文只写行为和一句话，没有更多交代；侯生所献窃符之计如何执行，证据未载。

The detail most worth doubting: the figure of eighty thousand picked men appears here alone, with no corroboration; how the tallies were verified in Jin Bi's camp goes unrecorded; Hou Ying's motive in cutting his own throat comes down to an act and a single sentence, with nothing further; and how Hou Ying's scheme to steal the tally was carried out is not recorded in the evidence.
本篇只有一个史源（《史记·魏公子列传》一处记述），对话与献计是史家记述，未必逐字；「心不快」「意驕矜」「立自責」是叙述用语而非实录心理；不换算公元年份；“得选兵八万人”仅此一处、无旁证；晋鄙军中合符如何校验原文未载；侯生自刭的动机原文只写行为与一句话；侯生所献窃符之计如何执行，证据未载。

This piece rests on a single historical source (one account in the Biography of the Wei Prince in the Records of the Grand Historian). The dialogue and the proposed scheme are the historian's rendering and need not be verbatim; the prince's displeasure, self-congratulation and self-blame are narrative labels rather than recorded psychology; years are not converted to the common era; the figure of eighty thousand picked men appears in this one place with no corroboration; how the tallies were verified in Jin Bi's camp is unrecorded in the source; Hou Ying's motive for cutting his own throat is given only as an act and a single sentence; how Hou Ying's scheme to steal the tally was carried out is not recorded in the evidence.
